Hi Evan — thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap and the data points we'd need to build a tailored cost estimate for BrightForge. Keeping this short so we can move to a worked example: 

Summary of what we discussed
- Volume ballpark: you mentioned "mid-hundreds of millions" of total monthly tokens and spiky daily traffic tied to product events. Please confirm a better monthly estimate if available.
- Cache strategy: you plan to use a prefix cache for system/boilerplate prompts plus per-user/local-session KV caching for recent context.
- Key ask from your side: target effective $/1M tokens (your budget band) and how caching assumptions change the effective unit cost.

Data we need from BrightForge to finalize an example pricing model
- Monthly raw token volume (approx): low/typical/high.
- Token distribution by request type (system, prompt, user message, completion) if you have it.
- Typical prompt length and average generated completion length (tokens).
- Any current estimates of prefix reuse rate or repeated prompts across users.

Our quick assumptions for the worked example below (we can update with your numbers):
- Baseline list price for hosted generation: $20 per 1M billed tokens (this is an example to illustrate unit economics; final quote will reflect committed capacity).
- Prefix cache hit-rate: 45% of prefix tokens (system + boilerplate) — these do not go to the model when served from cache.
- Overall effective cache hit-rate across all tokens (including short-term KV/session caching): 40%

What I'll produce next (action items)
1) Rishi (Cc'd) will produce a short worksheet showing billed vs raw token math for three volume bands.
2) Evan, if you can share a token histogram or a small sample log (CSV) we can run an exact calc.
3) I'll prepare 2 pricing scenarios (hosted with caching; dedicated/reserved capacity) and show effective $/1M tokens under 3 cache hit-rate cases (20%, 40%, 60%).

Attachments: request a quick token histogram (CSV) if possible. I've attached a sample worksheet template we can populate.

Next step: can we target Monday for the sample histogram? If not, I can run the example using the numbers you gave on the call.

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — cache assumptions & pricing examples

Hi Evan — thanks for the data. Below is a concise worked example using your 150M/month baseline and three cache hit-rate scenarios you asked for. I spell out both billed tokens (what appears on an invoice) and the effective cost per 1M raw tokens (what you should budget for).

Assumptions for this example
- Redwood example price (hosted, illustrative): $20 per 1M billed tokens
- Raw tokens (user-visible): 150,000,000 per month
- Effective billed tokens = Raw tokens * (1 - overall_cache_hit_rate)
- Effective $/1M raw tokens = (Billed tokens_in_M * unit_price) / (Raw tokens_in_M)

Scenario A — low cache (25% hit)
- Billed tokens = 150M * (1 - 0.25) = 112.5M billed
- Monthly cost = 112.5 * $20 = $2,250
- Effective $ per 1M raw tokens = $2,250 / 150 = $15.00 per 1M raw tokens

Scenario B — medium cache (45% hit)
- Billed tokens = 150M * (1 - 0.45) = 82.5M billed
- Monthly cost = 82.5 * $20 = $1,650
- Effective $ per 1M raw tokens = $1,650 / 150 = $11.00 per 1M raw tokens

Scenario C — high cache (65% hit)
- Billed tokens = 150M * (1 - 0.65) = 52.5M billed
- Monthly cost = 52.5 * $20 = $1,050
- Effective $ per 1M raw tokens = $1,050 / 150 = $7.00 per 1M raw tokens

Notes on prefix cache vs overall cache
- Prefix cache (system/boilerplate) typically affects only the prompt-side tokens. If system prompts are 20% of tokens and you have a 70% prefix hit on those, that alone reduces billed prompt tokens by 14% of total (0.2 * 0.7).
- Session/KV caching reduces recently repeated user tokens (e.g., multi-turn context). Those savings compound with prefix cache.
- The "overall_cache_hit_rate" we used above is the aggregate effect across all token types. When you provide a histogram we will compute a weighted hit-rate per token-type for more precise billing estimates.

How this maps to your $8–$15 target
- With a $20 baseline, achieving an effective $/1M in your $8–$15 band requires an overall cache hit-rate between roughly 25% and 65% (see scenarios). At 45% hit you land at ~$11/1M which is squarely in your band.

Next steps (concrete)
1) Rishi and I will take the token_histogram.csv and produce a worksheet with a per-token-type breakdown and a proposed quote for both hosted and dedicated (reserved capacity) pricing.
2) If you share a representative sample of prompts and completions, Rishi can simulate realistic prefix/cache hit mechanics and produce a more accurate effective invoice estimate.
3) I'll schedule a quick 30-minute follow-up next Tue to walk the numbers with your engineering lead unless you prefer a written worksheet first.

If this looks good I can also include a short sensitivity chart showing cost vs hit-rate so you can see marginal savings per 1% cache improvement.

Thanks — Marissa
